title: Koszul perfect objects represent cohomology classes on a principal open
statement: Let X=Spec(A) be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], let f_1,\ldots,f_r\in A, let U=D(f_1)\cup\cdots\cup D(f_r), and let E be an object of D_QCoh(O_X) [def-pc-derived-category]. For each e\ge1 let I_e\in D(O_X) be the object associated with the complex of A-modules I^\bullet(f_1^e,\ldots,f_r^e), defined by I^i=K^{i-1}(f_1^e,\ldots,f_r^e) for i\le0 and I^i=0 for i>0 (K^\bullet the cochain Koszul complex), so that there is a distinguished triangle I_e\to O_X\to K_e\to I_e[1] with u_e:I_e\to O_X the first map; the I_e form an inverse system I_1\leftarrow I_2\leftarrow\cdots compatible with the u_e. Then each I_e is perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex], each u_e|_U is an isomorphism, and the map colim_e Hom_{D(O_X)}(I_e,E)\to H^0(U,E|_U) sending \varphi:I_e\to E to \varphi|_U\circ(u_e|_U)^{-1}\in Hom_{D(O_U)}(O_U,E|_U)=H^0(U,E|_U) is an isomorphism.
